title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti until al dente, reserving 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, thinly slice the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat and gently cook the garlic until golden, about 3-4 minutes, being careful not to burn it.
Add red pepper flakes and cook for 30 seconds, then add the drained spaghetti along with a splash of the reserved pasta water.
Toss everything together over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until the sauce coats the noodles, adding more pasta water if needed.
Stir in parsley and parmesan, season with salt, and serve immediately.
storage_tips: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat gently with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.

title: Margherita Pizza
instructions: Preheat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet or pizza stone inside.
Stretch the pizza dough out on a floured surface into a 12-inch round.
Spread the crushed tomatoes evenly over the dough, leaving a border for the crust, and season with salt.
Tear the mozzarella into pieces and scatter over the sauce.
Carefully transfer the pizza onto the hot baking sheet and bake for 10-12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Top with fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil before slicing.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days and reheat well in a hot skillet or oven.

title: Chicken Parmesan
instructions: Pound the chicken breasts to an even thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station: beaten eggs in one bowl, breadcrumbs mixed with parmesan in another.
Dip each chicken breast in egg, then coat thoroughly in the breadcrumb mixture.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer the chicken to a baking dish, top with marinara sauce and mozzarella, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is melted and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest for a few minutes before serving, ideally over pasta.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days; reheat in the oven to keep the coating crisp.

title: Mushroom Risotto
instructions: Heat the vegetable stock in a saucepan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
In a large pan, heat olive oil and sauté the mushrooms until browned, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion and garlic until softened, then add the arborio rice and toast for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in the white wine and stir until absorbed, then begin adding the warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding more.
Continue for about 20 minutes until the rice is creamy and tender, then stir the mushrooms back in.
Remove from heat and stir in butter and parmesan before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh, but keeps in the fridge for 2 days; reheat gently with a splash of stock to restore creaminess.

title: Caprese Salad
instructions: Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a serving plate.
Tuck basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Season with salt and pepper just before serving.
storage_tips: Best served fresh; if needed, store components separately and assemble just before eating.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Cook the onion, carrot, and celery in a large pot until softened, then add the ground beef and brown thoroughly.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer the bolognese sauce for 30-40 minutes.
Meanwhile, make a béchamel by melting butter, whisking in flour, then gradually adding milk until thickened.
Cook the lasagna noodles according to package instructions and drain.
Layer noodles, bolognese sauce, béchamel, and mozzarella in a baking dish, repeating until ingredients are used, finishing with cheese on top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30-35 minutes until bubbling and golden, then rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days or freezes well for up to 3 months; reheat covered in the oven.

title: Minestrone Soup
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic until softened.
Add the diced tomatoes and vegetable stock, then bring to a simmer.
Stir in the kidney beans and zucchini and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and freezes well; pasta will soften further on reheating.

title: Chicken Piccata
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and dredge lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a skillet and cook the chicken for 2-3 minutes per side until golden; set aside.
In the same pan, cook garlic briefly, then add chicken stock, lemon juice, and capers, scraping up any browned bits.
Simmer the sauce for 3-4 minutes to reduce slightly, then whisk in the remaining butter.
Return the chicken to the pan and spoon the sauce over before serving.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days; reheat gently to avoid overcooking the chicken.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
instructions: Marinate the chicken in yogurt and half the garam masala for at least 30 minutes.
Melt butter in a large pot and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the marinated chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in tomato puree, chili powder, remaining garam masala, and salt, then simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Stir in the cream and simmer for another 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve with rice or naan.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; the sauce may thicken further on reheating.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the onion until golden.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in cumin, coriander, garam masala, and chili powder, cooking until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and salt, and simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Serve with rice or flatbread.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and freezes well; flavor improves the next day.

title: Vegetable Biryani
instructions: Soak the rice for 20 minutes, then parboil until about 70% cooked; drain and set aside.
Soak saffron in the warm milk and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot and fry the onion until golden brown; remove half for garnish.
Add garlic and ginger, then the mixed vegetables and biryani masala, and cook for 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt and mint, then layer the parboiled rice on top.
Drizzle the saffron milk over the rice, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is fully steamed.
Fluff gently and garnish with the reserved fried onions before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; reheat with a splash of water to keep the rice from drying out.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then blend into a smooth puree.
Heat oil in a pan and lightly fry the paneer cubes until golden; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until softened.
Add cumin, garam masala, and tomatoes, cooking until the mixture thickens slightly.
Stir in the spinach puree and salt, and simmer for 5-8 minutes.
Add the paneer back in along with the cream, and simmer for another 3 minutes before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; the sauce may separate slightly on reheating, so stir well.

title: Dal Tadka
instructions: Rinse the lentils and simmer with turmeric and salt in 3 cups of water until soft, about 20 minutes.
In a separate small pan, heat ghee and fry the cumin seeds and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic to the pan and cook until golden.
Stir in the tomato and cook for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Pour this tempering over the cooked lentils and stir to combine before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and freezes well.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions: Marinate the chicken in yogurt, half the garam masala, and paprika for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the marinated chicken until charred and cooked through; set aside.
In a pot, heat oil and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until soft.
Add the tomato puree, remaining garam masala, and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream and the cooked chicken, and simmer for another 5-8 minutes.
Serve with rice or naan.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well.

title: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and add cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in turmeric and coriander powder, then add the potatoes and cauliflower.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and garnish with cilantro before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; reheat in a pan to keep the texture from getting mushy.

title: Paneer Tikka
instructions: Mix yogurt, garam masala, chili powder, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, and salt into a marinade.
Toss the paneer, peppers, and onion in the marinade and let sit for at least 20 minutes.
Thread the paneer and vegetables onto skewers.
Grill or pan-sear over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until lightly charred, about 10-12 minutes.
Drizzle with a little oil before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh; keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days, though the paneer firms up when chilled.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch, and let sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until browned and cooked through; set aside.
In the same wok, quickly fry the dried chilies, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the wok, add the sauce and peanuts, and toss until everything is coated and glossy.
Garnish with green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; peanuts may soften slightly on reheating.

title: Vegetable Fried Rice
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Scramble the eggs quickly and set aside.
Add garlic and mixed vegetables to the wok and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, and scrambled eggs, tossing to combine.
Garnish with green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; reheat in a hot pan for the best texture.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and brown the ground pork thoroughly.
Add garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang, and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and soy sauce, then gently add the tofu cubes.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in a cornstarch-water slurry to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns and green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days; tofu texture softens further on reheating.

title: Beef and Broccoli
instructions: Toss the beef with 1 tbsp cornstarch and let sit for 10 minutes.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef quickly until browned; set aside.
Add garlic to the wok, then soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, and beef stock, and bring to a simmer.
Return the beef and broccoli to the wok and toss until the sauce thickens and coats everything.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; best reheated in a hot pan rather than the microwave.

title: Egg Drop Soup
instructions: Bring the stock to a simmer in a pot.
Mix the cornstarch with a little water and stir it into the stock to thicken slightly.
Slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs while stirring gently in one direction to form ribbons.
Season with white pepper and sesame oil.
Garnish with green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh; keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days, though the egg ribbons soften.

title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
instructions: Coat the chicken in beaten egg, then dredge in cornstarch.
Fry the chicken in batches until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
In a separate pan, whisk together ketchup, rice vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce, and bring to a simmer.
Add the bell peppers and pineapple, and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Toss the fried chicken in the sauce until well coated before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; the coating softens on reheating.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
instructions: Cook the noodles according to package instructions, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan and brown the ground pork with garlic until crispy.
In each serving bowl, mix chili oil, sesame paste, soy sauce, black vinegar, and Sichuan peppercorns.
Add the cooked noodles to the bowls and toss with the sauce.
Top with the pork and green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh; store noodles and sauce separately if planning to keep leftovers.

title: Vegetable Spring Rolls
instructions: Heat a little oil in a pan and stir-fry the cabbage, carrot, mushrooms, and garlic until softened.
Season the filling with soy sauce and sesame oil, then let it cool slightly.
Place a spoonful of filling on each spring roll wrapper and roll tightly, sealing the edge with water.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C) and fry the rolls in batches until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh and crisp; keeps in the fridge for 2 days, though reheating in an oven or air fryer restores crispness better than a microwave.

title: Chicken Katsu
instructions: Pound the chicken breasts to an even thickness and season with salt.
Dredge each breast in flour, then egg, then coat thoroughly in panko.
Heat oil in a skillet and fry the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and slice into strips.
Serve with katsu sauce and steamed rice.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat in an oven or air fryer to keep the coating crisp.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Heat the dashi stock in a pot until warm but not boiling.
Ladle a little hot stock into a bowl and whisk in the miso paste until smooth, then return it to the pot.
Add the tofu and wakame, and warm through gently without boiling.
Garnish with green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh, as tofu texture changes on reheating; keeps in the fridge for 1-2 days.

title: Teriyaki Salmon
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sugar, garlic, and ginger to make the teriyaki sauce.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and sear the salmon skin-side down for 4 minutes.
Flip the salmon and pour the sauce over it, simmering for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens and glazes the fish.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently to avoid drying out the fish.

title: Vegetable Yakisoba
instructions: Loosen the noodles under warm water if needed and set aside.
Heat oil in a large skillet and stir-fry the cabbage, carrot, and bell pepper until just tender.
Add the noodles to the skillet and toss to combine with the vegetables.
Pour in the yakisoba sauce and toss everything together until evenly coated.
Garnish with green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat in a hot pan to keep the noodles from getting soggy.

title: Onigiri (Rice Balls)
instructions: Wet your hands with water and a little salt to prevent sticking.
Take a handful of warm rice and flatten it slightly in your palm.
Press a piece of umeboshi into the center and fold the rice around it.
Shape into a triangle or ball, pressing firmly so it holds together.
Wrap a strip of nori around the base and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
storage_tips: Best eaten the same day at room temperature; refrigeration makes the rice hard, though it keeps for up to 1 day.

title: Gyoza (Pan-Fried Dumplings)
instructions: Mix the pork, cabbage, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and sesame oil into a filling.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper, wet the edges, and fold into a pleated half-moon shape.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and arrange the dumplings flat-side down.
Fry for 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden, then add the water and cover to steam for 5-6 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook until the water evaporates and the bottoms crisp up again before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days, or freeze uncooked dumplings for up to 2 months.

title: Chicken Donburi (Oyakodon)
instructions: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a skillet and bring to a simmer.
Add the onion and chicken, and cook until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Beat the eggs and pour them evenly over the chicken mixture, cover, and cook until the eggs are just set.
Spoon the chicken and egg mixture over bowls of steamed rice.
Garnish with green onions before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh, as the egg texture changes on reheating; keeps in the fridge for 1-2 days.

title: Agedashi Tofu
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Dust each cube lightly with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the tofu cubes until golden and crisp on all sides.
Warm the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin together in a small pot.
Place the fried tofu in a bowl, pour the warm sauce over it, and top with green onions and grated daikon.
storage_tips: Best served immediately, as the tofu loses crispness quickly; not recommended for storage.

title: Chicken Tacos
instructions: Season the chicken with taco seasoning.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or over an open flame.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, onion, and cilantro.
Serve with lime wedges.
storage_tips: Keep chicken and tortillas separate in the fridge for up to 3 days; assemble tacos fresh before eating.

title: Vegetarian Black Bean Burrito
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the black beans, cumin, and chili powder, and cook for 5 minutes, mashing some of the beans slightly.
Warm the tortillas and rice.
Layer rice, bean mixture, and salsa in the center of each tortilla.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a burrito.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; wrap tightly in foil to reheat evenly.

title: Beef Enchiladas
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion until softened, then add the ground beef and brown thoroughly.
Season the beef with cumin and chili powder.
Warm the tortillas slightly to make them pliable, then fill each with beef and a little cheese, and roll tightly.
Arrange the rolled tortillas seam-side down in a baking dish and pour the enchilada sauce over the top.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes until bubbling.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well before baking.

title: Guacamole & Chips
instructions: Mash the avocados in a bowl to your preferred consistency.
Stir in lime juice, onion, tomato, and cilantro.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.
storage_tips: Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to limit browning; best eaten within 1 day.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until the skins are charred, then steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes and peel.
Make a small slit in each pepper and remove the seeds, then stuff with cheese.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold in the yolks.
Dust each stuffed pepper with flour, dip in the egg batter, and fry in hot oil until golden on all sides.
Warm the tomato sauce and serve the peppers topped with sauce.
storage_tips: Best fresh, as the batter softens; keeps in the fridge for 1-2 days.

title: Pozole Rojo
instructions: Simmer the pork with onion, garlic, bay leaves, and water to cover for about 1 hour until tender, then shred and reserve the broth.
Rehydrate the dried chilies in hot water, then blend into a smooth paste with a little broth.
Strain the chili paste into the broth along with the shredded pork and oregano, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the hominy and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Serve topped with shredded cabbage, radishes, and lime wedges.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; add fresh toppings after reheating.

title: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
instructions: Grill the corn over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until charred in spots, about 10-12 minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise and sour cream together.
Brush the grilled corn generously with the mayonnaise mixture.
Sprinkle with cotija cheese and chili powder.
Squeeze lime juice over the top and garnish with cilantro before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh off the grill; leftover corn can be refrigerated and toppings added fresh.

title: Chicken Fajitas
instructions: Toss the chicken with fajita seasoning.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat and cook the chicken until browned and cooked through; set aside.
In the same skillet, stir-fry the peppers and onion until softened with a slight char.
Return the chicken to the skillet and toss everything together with a squeeze of lime.
Serve with warm tortillas.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat in a hot skillet to restore some char.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the zucchini and bell peppers, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, herbes de Provence, and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the flavors meld.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and tastes even better the next day; freezes well.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Brown the chicken pieces in the bacon fat on all sides, then remove.
Sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms in the same pot until golden.
Stir in the flour, then add the wine and stock, scraping up any browned bits.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot along with garlic and thyme, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Finish by stirring in the butter for a glossy sauce before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; flavor deepens overnight.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and cook the onions over low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized.
Add the sherry and cook for 1-2 minutes to deglaze the pot.
Pour in the stock and thyme, and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Season with salt, then ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls.
Top each bowl with a baguette slice and a generous layer of gruyere.
Broil until the cheese is melted and bubbling before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days without the bread topping; add fresh bread and cheese when reheating.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and blind-bake the pie crust for 10 minutes.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp and drain on paper towels.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, nutmeg, and salt.
Scatter the bacon and cheese evenly over the crust, then pour the egg mixture on top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until the filling is set and lightly golden.
Let cool for 10 minutes before slicing.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; reheat slices in the oven to keep the crust crisp.

title: Croque Monsieur
instructions: Melt butter in a small saucepan, whisk in flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook until thickened into a béchamel, then season with nutmeg.
Assemble sandwiches with ham and half the cheese between the bread slices.
Toast the sandwiches in a skillet with butter until golden on both sides.
Top each sandwich with béchamel and remaining cheese, then broil briefly until bubbling.
storage_tips: Best fresh; the béchamel doesn't reheat well, so this is not ideal for leftovers.

title: Beef Bourguignon
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat, then remove.
Sauté the carrots and onion until softened, then stir in the garlic and flour.
Add the tomato paste, wine, and stock, scraping up any browned bits, then return the beef and bacon to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours until the beef is very tender.
Stir in the mushrooms in the last 20 minutes of cooking.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; flavor improves overnight.

title: Salade Niçoise
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, then set aside to cool slightly.
Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then plunge into cold water.
Boil the eggs to your preferred doneness, then peel and halve.
Whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, and mustard for the dressing.
Arrange the tuna, potatoes, green beans, tomatoes, olives, and eggs on a platter.
Drizzle with the dressing just before serving.
storage_tips: Best assembled fresh; components can be prepped and refrigerated separately for up to 2 days.

title: Vichyssoise (Leek and Potato Soup)
instructions: Melt butter in a pot and sauté the leeks until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the potatoes and vegetable stock, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are very tender.
Blend the soup until smooth using an immersion or standard blender.
Stir in the cream and season with salt.
Chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours if serving cold, or serve warm, garnished with chives.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; can be served hot or cold.

title: Classic Cheeseburger
instructions: Divide the ground beef into 4 patties and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat a skillet or grill over medium-high heat and cook the patties for 3-4 minutes per side for medium doneness.
Add a slice of cheese to each patty in the last minute of cooking to melt.
Toast the buns lightly.
Assemble the burgers with lettuce, tomato, and onion.
storage_tips: Cooked patties keep in the fridge for up to 3 days; assemble fresh to avoid soggy buns.

title: BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwich
instructions: Rub the pork shoulder generously with the bbq rub and let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the pork in a slow cooker or covered oven at 300°F (150°C) for 3.5-4 hours until it shreds easily with a fork.
Shred the pork and mix with some of its cooking juices.
Toss the shredded pork with bbq sauce.
Pile onto buns and top with coleslaw.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; reheat gently with a splash of sauce to keep it moist.

title: Mac and Cheese
instructions: Cook the macaroni according to package instructions and drain.
Melt butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook until thickened into a smooth sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in the cheese until melted, then season with salt and paprika.
Combine the sauce with the cooked macaroni and serve.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; add a splash of milk when reheating to loosen the sauce.

title: Buffalo Chicken Wings
instructions: Toss the wings with baking powder and salt, then arrange on a wire rack.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 40-45 minutes, flipping halfway, until crispy.
Melt the butter and whisk in the hot sauce and garlic powder.
Toss the baked wings in the sauce until fully coated.
Serve with celery sticks and your choice of dip.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat in the oven to restore crispness.

title: Cobb Salad
instructions: Arrange the chopped lettuce on a large platter as the base.
Arrange rows of chicken, bacon, eggs, tomatoes, blue cheese, and avocado on top.
Drizzle with ranch dressing just before serving, or serve on the side.
storage_tips: Best assembled fresh; components can be prepped and stored separately for up to 2 days.

title: Meatloaf
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix the ground beef, breadcrumbs, eggs, onion, worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into a loaf and place in a baking dish.
Spread ketchup evenly over the top.
Bake for 60-65 minutes until cooked through, then rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well, sliced or whole.

title: Clam Chowder
instructions: Cook the bacon in a pot until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Sauté the onion and celery in the bacon fat until softened.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually add the milk and clam juice, stirring to avoid lumps.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15-20 minutes until tender.
Stir in the clams, cream, and bacon, and heat through without boiling before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat gently over low heat to avoid curdling the cream.

title: Grilled Cheese & Tomato Soup
instructions: Simmer the crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock, and garlic in a pot for 15 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth, then stir in the cream and season to taste.
Butter the outside of the bread slices and assemble sandwiches with cheese in the middle.
Grill the sandwiches in a skillet over medium heat until golden and the cheese is melted, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve the sandwiches alongside bowls of the tomato soup.
storage_tips: Soup keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days; grilled cheese is best made fresh.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: Combine the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano.
Toss the salad with the dressing.
Top with feta cheese just before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day, though the vegetables release liquid over time.

title: Chicken Souvlaki
instructions: Marinate the chicken in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and oregano for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the chicken onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until cooked through and lightly charred.
Warm the pita bread.
Serve the skewers with pita and tzatziki.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat gently to avoid drying out the chicken.

title: Falafel Wrap
instructions: Pulse the soaked (uncooked) chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, and coriander in a food processor until finely ground but not pureed.
Stir in the flour and let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
Shape into small balls or patties.
Heat oil in a pot and fry the falafel in batches until deeply golden and crisp, about 3-4 minutes.
Serve in warm flatbreads with tahini sauce and fresh vegetables.
storage_tips: Cooked falafel keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; reheat in an oven to restore crispness.

title: Hummus
instructions: Combine the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt in a food processor.
Blend until smooth, adding a little water as needed to reach a creamy consistency.
Transfer to a bowl and drizzle with olive oil before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days in an airtight container.

title: Greek Moussaka
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices and let sit for 20 minutes to draw out moisture, then pat dry.
Brush the eggplant with olive oil and roast or grill until softened.
Cook the onion and garlic, then brown the ground lamb and stir in the tomatoes and cinnamon, simmering for 20 minutes.
Make a béchamel by melting butter, whisking in flour, then gradually adding milk until thickened; stir in parmesan.
Layer the eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, top with béchamel.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35-40 minutes until golden on top, then rest for 10 minutes before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika, cooking until fragrant.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10-15 minutes until slightly thickened.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set but yolks are still soft, about 6-8 minutes.
Top with feta and cilantro before serving.
storage_tips: Best fresh, as the eggs overcook on reheating; the tomato base alone keeps for up to 3 days.

title: Tabbouleh
instructions: Soak the bulgur in hot water for 15-20 minutes until softened, then drain well.
Combine the bulgur with parsley, mint, and tomatoes in a large bowl.
Whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, and salt.
Toss the salad with the dressing and let sit for a few minutes before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; flavor improves after a few hours.

title: Grilled Branzino
instructions: Pat the fish dry and season the cavity and outside with salt.
Stuff each fish with lemon slices, garlic, and rosemary.
Rub the outside with olive oil.
Grill over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes per side until the flesh flakes easily.
Serve whole or filet before plating.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for up to 1 day.

title: Chicken Shawarma
instructions: Marinate the chicken in yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, and turmeric for at least 1 hour.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and cook the chicken over medium-high heat until charred and cooked through, about 12-15 minutes.
Slice the chicken thinly.
Warm the pita bread.
Serve the sliced chicken in pita with tahini sauce and fresh vegetables.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat gently to avoid drying out.

title: Fattoush Salad
instructions: Toast or fry the pita bread until crisp, then break into pieces.
Combine the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, and radishes in a large bowl.
Whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, sumac, and salt.
Toss the salad with the dressing.
Top with the crispy pita pieces just before serving.
storage_tips: Best assembled fresh, as the pita softens quickly; store dressing and salad separately for up to 2 days.

title: Baba Ganoush
instructions: Roast or grill the whole eggplants over direct flame or in a hot oven until the skin is charred and the flesh is very soft, about 25-30 minutes.
Let the eggplants cool slightly, then scoop out the flesh, discarding the skin.
Mash or blend the eggplant flesh with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt.
Transfer to a bowl and drizzle with olive oil.
Garnish with parsley before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Kofta Kebabs
instructions: Combine the ground lamb, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and salt in a bowl, mixing until well combined.
Shape the mixture around skewers into long oval kebabs.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until cooked through and charred in spots.
Rest briefly before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days and freezes well raw or cooked.

title: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice)
instructions: Cook the lentils in water until just tender, about 15-20 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the onions until deeply caramelized and crispy; set aside on paper towels.
In a pot, combine the lentils, rice, cumin, salt, and 2 cups of water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fluff and top with the crispy onions before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; the crispy onions are best stored separately.

title: Manakish Za'atar
instructions: Preheat the oven to 475°F (245°C).
Divide the dough into 4 portions and roll each into a thin round.
Mix the za'atar with olive oil to form a spreadable paste.
Spread the za'atar mixture generously over each dough round.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until the edges are golden and the base is cooked through.
storage_tips: Best fresh and warm; keeps for up to 2 days and reheats well in a hot oven.

title: Maqluba
instructions: Fry the eggplant and cauliflower slices in oil until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Simmer the chicken with onion, cinnamon, and allspice in water until cooked through, then remove the chicken and reserve the broth.
Layer the fried vegetables and chicken in a large pot, then top with the rinsed rice.
Pour in the reserved broth to just cover the rice, cover the pot, and simmer on low for 25-30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Let rest for 10 minutes, then carefully invert the pot onto a large serving platter.
Garnish with toasted pine nuts before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat gently to keep the layers intact.

title: Stuffed Grape Leaves (Warak Enab)
instructions: Rinse the grape leaves to remove excess brine.
Mix the rice, tomatoes, parsley, mint, half the olive oil, and salt for the filling.
Place a spoonful of filling near the stem end of each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Arrange the rolls snugly in a pot, seam-side down, and pour over the remaining olive oil, lemon juice, and enough water to just cover.
Place a small plate on top to keep the rolls submerged, cover, and simmer on low for 40-45 minutes until the rice is tender.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days; can be served warm or cold.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot and brown the chicken pieces on all sides; set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the same pot until softened.
Stir in ginger, cinnamon, and turmeric, then return the chicken to the pot.
Add the apricots, olives, preserved lemon, and stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 45-50 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; flavors deepen overnight.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the canned tomatoes, bell pepper, half the onion, and scotch bonnet into a smooth puree.
Heat oil in a large pot and fry the tomato paste and remaining diced onion for a few minutes.
Add the blended tomato mixture and cook down for 15-20 minutes until thickened and the raw taste is gone.
Stir in curry powder, bay leaves, and chicken stock, then add the rinsed rice.
Cover and cook on low heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the sauce.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; reheat with a splash of water or stock.

title: Doro Wat (Ethiopian Chicken Stew)
instructions: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium heat, stirring frequently, until deeply softened and lightly browned, about 15-20 minutes.
Add the butter, garlic, and ginger, and cook for a few minutes.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken stock and chicken pieces, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Add the hard-boiled eggs in the last 10 minutes to warm through and absorb the sauce.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and freezes well; flavor improves the next day.

title: Egyptian Koshari
instructions: Cook the lentils, rice, and pasta separately according to package/standard instructions, then combine in a large bowl with the chickpeas.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until deeply crisp and golden; set aside.
Make the tomato sauce by cooking garlic in a little oil, then adding the crushed tomatoes, cumin, and vinegar, and simmering for 15 minutes.
Serve the lentil-rice-pasta mixture topped with tomato sauce and crispy onions.
storage_tips: Keeps components separately in the fridge for up to 4 days; combine fresh when serving.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion until softened, then add the ground beef and brown thoroughly.
Stir in curry powder, the soaked bread (mashed in), and dried apricots.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and press it into an even layer, tucking in bay leaves.
Whisk together the eggs and milk, then pour over the meat mixture.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30-35 minutes until the custard topping is set and golden.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat gently to avoid overcooking the custard top.

title: West African Peanut Stew
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the sweet potatoes, crushed tomatoes, chili powder, and vegetable stock, and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 15-20 minutes until the sweet potatoes are nearly tender.
Whisk in the peanut butter until fully incorporated.
Stir in the kale and simmer for another 5 minutes until wilted before serving.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and freezes well; the peanut base thickens further when chilled.

title: Moroccan Couscous with Vegetables
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté the onion and carrots until slightly softened.
Add the zucchini, chickpeas, cumin, and cinnamon, and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in half the vegetable stock and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring the remaining stock to a boil, pour over the couscous, cover, and let sit for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Stir the raisins into the vegetable mixture and serve over the couscous.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; reheat with a splash of stock or water.

title: Nigerian Suya (Spiced Grilled Beef Skewers)
instructions: Mix the ground peanuts, paprika, cayenne, ginger powder, garlic powder, and onion powder to make the suya spice blend.
Toss the beef slices with vegetable oil, then coat generously with the spice blend.
Thread the beef onto skewers.
Grill over high heat for 2-3 minutes per side until charred and cooked to your liking.
Serve with sliced raw onion.
storage_tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat briefly on a hot pan to restore some char.
